messages:
Tom R.: Morning folks — daycare called, center closed for 2 days due to water issue. I need to be home tomorrow and Friday to care for my toddler. Im also scheduled to start formal parental leave in 6 weeks; want to make sure this short absence is handled cleanly (payroll/timeoff + oncall coverage).

Emily (Manager): Oh no, hope it's minor. Tom, you can take short-term family care. For oncall I can swap you out for those two days. Please post a 1-line handoff and mark time in Workday.

Tom R.: Will do. Quick Q: can I convert to emergency dependent care (EDC) or should I use PTO? Prefer not to burn my accrued parental leave bank.

People Ops - Priya: Hi Tom — EDC is meant for short unexpected caregiver events and won't affect your approved parental leave start date or accruals. Steps: 1) submit the Emergency Care form within 72h, 2) mark time as "EDC" in Workday (we have a separate code), 3) payroll will apply stipend per policy. If you prefer PTO we can also convert it.

Tom R.: Is there a hard limit on EDC days per year?

People Ops - Priya: Yes, policy allows up to 10 days per rolling 12 months for emergency dependent care. If you exceed that, we'll discuss unpaid leave or PTO.

Tom R.: Got it. Also need to confirm: if I work partially remote (half days) tomorrow, is that ok for EDC?

Benefits Bot: Hybrid/partial day guidance: EDC is for days where caregiving prevents regular work. If you can perform at least 50% of normal duties, consider marking partial day PTO + remote status. Team leads approve exceptions.

Emily (Manager): Tom — feel free to do half-days if that helps. Ping for urgent context; I'll cover oncall full day.

Tom R.: Thanks. Posting a handoff now:

```
Handoff: Tom R. OOO 3/soon (daycare closure) — Emily (manager) covering. In-flight items: #452 deploy to staging blocked on infra review; PR: https://.../pr/789; Customer A demo scheduled 3/05 (Emily to run). Slack: #eng-team. No expected paging unless production latent errors.
```

Facilities - Jana: FYI weve escalated the water issue at the daycare vendor (BrightStart). Estimated re-open: Friday afternoon.

Tom R.: Priya I submitted the Emergency Care form: https://hr.redwood.example.com/forms/EDC/submit/1880124680 (internal). Can you confirm receipt?

People Ops - Priya: Received. Case ID: EDC-2026-472. Ive flagged it as expedited. Payroll will include stipend in next pay cycle if processed before payroll lock.

Payroll Bot: Payroll update: EDC case EDC-2026-472 logged. Status: awaiting manager verification. Please ensure Workday entry before EOD.

Tom R.: Workday entry done (EDC code) for 2 days.

Emily (Manager): Verified EDC entries. Approved.

People Ops - Priya: All set from HR side. Note for record: short EDC days do not change parental leave start date. If you later want to shift your formal parental leave start date, submit a leave amendment.

Tom R.: One final ask — will these EDC days affect my benefits/prorated parental pay calculations?

Benefits Bot: Short paid EDC days are treated as paid company time and do not reduce benefit accruals or change prorated parental pay calculations. Only unpaid leave or extended FMLA-style absences alter prorata calculations.

Tom R.: Great, thanks everyone. Appreciate quick responses.

People Ops - Priya: Glad we could help. If anything changes (extension >5 days) ping me and we'll open backfill and payroll priority. :heart:
